memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then he spoke his message: "Arise, Balak, and listen; hear me, son of Zippor. God is not human, that he should lie, not a human being, that he should change his mind. Does he speak and then not act? Does he promise and not fulfil?" - Num 23:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam's second oracle opens with one of the most magnificent statements about God in all of Scripture. God is not human, that He should lie, nor a mortal, that He should change His mind. Unlike people, who break their word and shift their plans, God always does what He says. When He speaks, He acts. When He promises, He fulfils.

Think of how often human promises fail us. People make commitments they do not keep, say things they do not mean, and change their minds when it suits them. We have all been let down by broken words. But God is utterly unlike this. His character is truth itself, and His word is completely reliable.

This truth is meant to steady our souls. Every promise God has made, He will keep. Not one of His words will fall to the ground. Where human faithfulness falters, God's faithfulness stands firm forever. He cannot lie, and He will not fail.

This is the bedrock of our confidence in Christ. In Him, every one of God's promises is "Yes" and "Amen" (2 Cor 1:20). The God who cannot lie has promised eternal life to all who trust His Son (Titus 1:2). When doubts assail you, return to this rock: God does not lie, and He does not fail to fulfil His word.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it comfort you that God cannot lie or break His promises?
2. Which promise of God do you most need to trust today?
3. How does God's faithfulness contrast with the broken promises you have known?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that You never lie and never fail to keep Your word. When doubts arise, anchor me in the certainty that every promise You have made in Christ is sure. Amen.
